title: Definitional normal forms: short formulas with fresh atoms
summary: Introduce names for subformula values and convert formulas to short clause lists, preserving satisfiability by explicit extension and restriction of valuations.
abstract: Turning a formula into a conjunction of clauses can make it much longer. A different approach gives each subformula a new name and writes a few short clauses explaining what that name means. The resulting clauses describe the original calculation one connective at a time. We prove that every satisfying assignment to the original atoms extends to a satisfying assignment to these clauses, and every satisfying assignment to the clauses gives one for the original formula. The new names are forced where they are used, and the numbers of clauses and literal occurrences grow at most linearly with the formula tree.
